messages:
morgan: FYI — noticed a correlated spike after last-night's BMC firmware push to ap-south1 racks. OOB sessions dropping intermittently and some hosts flipping secure-boot state during coldreboot. GPU provisioning backlog starting to grow. :warning:

deploy-bot: deployment 2026-03-19T02:11Z completed for bmc-fw v2.14 -> ap-south1 (canary=10%, ramp=50%).

kai: Seeing allocation errors in the provisioner: `ERR: secure boot state mismatch (expected=enabled, actual=disabled)`. ~120 GPU alloc fails in the last 20m, mostly rack-tag=apse3-edge-0{3..7}.

anya: Can we pause the rollout? If the BMC toggles NVRAM keys on coldboot we risk large-scale evictions. Recommend hold and roll back canary to v2.13 for affected racks. :hand:

sam: Rolling back BMC fw on hundreds of boards will cause additional cold reboots. That could extend downtime for jobs on those nodes. Alternative: isolate racks by tag, mark as unschedulable and drain, then fallback.

devon: If we mark them unschedulable we should also temporarily divert queued GPU jobs to us-central1-dedicated pools. Cost will go up but preserves customer SLAs.

finance-bot: alert: cross-region burst to us-central1 estimated incremental cost ~+$2.3k/day at current runrate. Confirm before large-scale migration.

jess: Quick triage commands: `oobctl get sessions --rack=apse3-edge-05 --json | jq '.sessions[] | {id,state,secureBoot}'` and `redwood-provisioner metrics series --name=alloc_failures --region=ap-south1 --last=30m`. Also check `ipmi sensor` for any power churn.

kai: Ran `oobctl` — sample from apse3-edge-05: `{id: "oob-4432", state: "connected", secureBoot: "disabled"}`. Previous firmware had NVRAM policy default-enabled; looks like v2.14 accidentally resets the UEFI boot order in some vendor images.

morgan: OK let's do this: 1) pause rollout immediately, 2) add tag `bmc-rollback-pending` to affected racks, 3) drain and cordon them, 4) kick short-term relocation for high-priority jobs. Who's actioning rollback/runbook?

anya: I'll take rollback coordination. Plan: run rollback playbook for the 6 affected racks, start sequentially, watch OOB session retention metric. Need eng-oncall and infra-sre on standby.

sam: I'll script the drain with a 5-min grace and move pending pods via scheduler hints. Also adding a temporary route to reduce OOB session churn (lower keepalive to 30s).

eng-oncall: @anya @sam acknowledged. Turning on extra pager coverage for the next 6 hours. If rollbacks fail >2 racks escalate to hardware vendor.

devon: I'll open a low-latency migration window and throttle migrations to keep costs under control — aim to cap cross-region at 200 GPUs/hr.

finance-bot: noted budget cap; if we exceed threshold, auto-notify @finance.

morgan: Good. Post-mortem timeline requested: include root cause (nvram reset), exact rack list, per-rack SDK logs, and any vendor image variants. Also add a mitigation: vendor kernel/fw gating in CI before rollout.

jess: Adding checklist to runbook: verify `secureBoot` persisted after two cold reboots, validate UEFI vars with `efivar -l`, and ensure BMC NVRAM write path uses non-destructive flag.

kai: For visibility I'm pushing a short dashboard panel for `alloc_failures_by_rack` and `oob_session_disconnect_rate`. Will share link in 10m. :mag:

morgan: Thanks everyone — pause is in effect, rollback plan in motion. Will update when first rack is back in service. :thumbsup:
